question.text: An elevator in a building can carry a maximum of <math><mn>10</mn></math> persons, with the average mass of each person being <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>68</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> . The mass of the elevator itself is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>920</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and it moves with a constant speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> . The frictional force opposing the motion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> . If the elevator is moving up with its full capacity, the power delivered by the motor to the elevator <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfenced></math> must be at least:

solution.text:
Net force on motor will be
Fm=920+6810g+6000
=22000 N
So, required power for motor
Pm=F→m.v→
=22000×3
=66000 watt
